series.title: Road to protocol-v3
series.description: How p2party evolved from uniform encrypted chunks into a browser-native hybrid post-quantum Double Ratchet, and what the metadata-privacy research still has to prove.

posts.title: The 64 KiB lie: how p2party learned to make every chunk look guilty
posts.description: Uniform chunks, decoys, message-scoped WebRTC channels, and the bugs that taught us what fixed-size encryption does not hide.

posts.title: Green tests are not a security proof
posts.description: The impossible nonce, fail-open DTLS check, ratchet desynchronization, and key-separation traps that adversarial review caught.

posts.title: A room is n-1 sessions wearing one URL
posts.description: The signaling star, full WebRTC mesh, message-scoped channels, transport-neutral createSession API, and fragment room invites.

posts.title: Protocol-v3 is not PQXDH, X-Wing, or a pile of fashionable acronyms
posts.description: The exact live-edge handshake: separate identities, interactive 3DH, room-selected ML-KEM, optional CPace, and chained confirmation.

posts.title: Free is a dangerous word: the Double Ratchet, sparse PQ healing, and the cells we already paid for
posts.description: What ships, what remains gated, and the measured systems claim across cover traffic, blind rendezvous, and private swarms.

posts.title: Borrowing from SPQR: what a sparse post-quantum ratchet costs when you cannot chunk the ciphertext
posts.description: Signal's SPQR fragments ML-KEM across many messages. p2party's cells already fit one whole. Same problem, inverted constraint - and why none of Signal's analysis transfers.

posts.title: An open channel is not a live peer: the phone that slept through its own disconnection
posts.description: Binding every peer edge to the DTLS certificate it was authenticated against, the four smaller lies that fell out of it, and the SIGSTOP harness that had to agree first.
